text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific Dunlop Ltd said on Firday it expected an improved trading result for the year to June 30, 1997, although the frist six months would be below the previous year.
Pacific Dunlop earlier announced a net loss of A$132.7 million after abnormal losses of A$284.55 million.

"This year the company is anticipating an improved full year trading result. However, results for the current six months will be below the first half of last year," Pacific Dunlop chairman John Gough said in a statement.
Gough said the last two years have been among the 'most difficult' in Pacific Dunlop's history.

"The experience of the last two years has been sobering, but in managing our way through it Pacific Dunlop is today in a position to look to future growth, and this will unfold over the next two years," Gough said.
Managing director Rod Chadwick said Pacific Dunlop enters 1996/97 with a streamlined group of operations in three categories.
One, manufacturing, groups GNB Technologies, Ansell International, Cables and South Pacific Tyres.
"In these businesses scale is very important. Growth wil be derived from investment and acquisitions that contribute to either global or regional leadership," Chadwick said.
Chadwick said the second category is distribution, which groups automotive and electrical distribution.
The third category is the consumer products group, Pacific Brands.
At 3.18 p.m. (0518 GMT), Pacific Dunlop shares were seven cents up at A$2.72.
